correctness.rationale: If K is the candidate's worst relative width, then pointwise g(s) is bounded above by K z_alpha sqrt(s). The candidate crossing event is therefore contained in the crossing event for that square-root envelope. Calibration forces K z_alpha to be at least the 1-alpha quantile of sup |W(s)|/sqrt(s), and choosing the square-root boundary at that quantile attains equality. This is a complete continuum proof and does not rely on the package's finite-grid sanity check.

value.rationale: Worst multiplicative precision loss versus ordinary fixed-time inference is a natural repeated-inference design criterion. The theorem turns the familiar square-root/Pocock shape from one member of a parametric family into a global optimizer over all deterministic Brownian boundaries for that criterion, while clearly separating this objective from power or stopping time.

final_claim: Among all deterministic Brownian boundaries on a fixed bounded horizon with simultaneous coverage at least 1-alpha, the square-root boundary globally minimizes the worst half-width relative to the corresponding fixed-time Gaussian interval, with optimal ratio c_alpha(Delta)/z_alpha; in the Confidence Horizons power family this is q=1/2.
limitations: Asymptotic Brownian setting, deterministic pre-specified boundaries and one specific worst-width loss.
No uniqueness claim and no finite-sample confidence-sequence guarantee.
